title: Bring-up & Validation
description: Checks for first boards back, from receiving inspection through power-on, functional bring-up and design validation before releasing the next revision.

items.text: Received boards match the ordered revision, quantity and assembly variant
items.hint: Check the silkscreen revision, fab date code and assembly variant label against the purchase order and release package. Mixed revisions in one batch cause confusing bring-up results.

items.text: Each board has a unique serial number or label recorded in the bring-up log
items.hint: Results, rework and failures must be traceable to a specific unit. Label boards before anyone starts probing.

items.text: Visual inspection shows no solder bridges, tombstones, missing or misplaced parts
items.hint: Inspect under magnification against the assembly drawing; use IPC-A-610 as the acceptance reference. Pay particular attention to fine-pitch leads and QFN edges.

items.text: Polarized parts (diodes, electrolytic and tantalum capacitors, LEDs) are fitted in the correct orientation
items.hint: Compare each polarity mark to the assembly drawing, not just the silkscreen, since silkscreen marks are sometimes wrong. A reversed tantalum can fail short on first power.

items.text: Pin-1 orientation of every IC and connector matches the assembly drawing
items.hint: Check ICs, regulators, crystals with polarity and keyed connectors. A rotated regulator or MCU usually damages itself or the rail on power-up.

items.text: Do-not-fit (DNF) positions are unpopulated and fitted options match the build variant
items.hint: Walk the BOM's DNF list and variant table. A fitted DNF strap or resistor can short rails or select the wrong mode.

items.text: Bare-board dimensions, hole positions and mounting features match the fabrication drawing
items.hint: Measure board outline and key mounting holes with calipers, and trial-fit into the enclosure or mechanical fixture if available.

items.text: X-ray inspection report for BGA and bottom-terminated parts shows acceptable voiding and no bridges or opens
items.hint: Request X-ray images for every BGA/LGA/QFN thermal pad. Compare voiding to the assembler's acceptance criteria; open balls often show as missing joints in the image.

items.text: Flex sections are free of cracks, delamination and coverlay damage at the bend regions
items.hint: Inspect stiffener edges and the rigid-flex transition under magnification. Do not flex the board beyond its specified bend radius during handling.

items.text: Conformal coating (if applied) covers the intended areas and keep-out areas such as connectors and test points are clean
items.hint: Inspect under UV light if the coating has a tracer. Coating on connector contacts or test pads causes intermittent contact.

items.text: Resistance from each power rail to ground is measured and recorded on an unpowered board
items.hint: Measure every rail at a test point or capacitor with a DMM, observing meter polarity. Compare across boards; an outlier points to a short or a missing part.

items.text: No rail measures a hard short (near 0 Ω) to ground or to another rail
items.hint: Large-capacitance or low-voltage core rails can read low ohms legitimately; compare against a known-good board or the expected load. Locate shorts with a thermal camera at very low current limit or a milliohm meter.

items.text: Input power connector polarity and pinout are verified against the schematic
items.hint: Check with a continuity meter from connector pins to the input protection and ground. A mirrored connector footprint is a common first-article error.

items.text: Jumpers, straps, DIP switches and boot-mode resistors are set to the bring-up configuration
items.hint: Document the configuration used in the bring-up log. Default boot from an unprogrammed external flash may need a strap change to enter the debugger or ROM bootloader.

items.text: Rail-to-rail resistance shows no unexpected low-impedance paths between rails
items.hint: Check pairs of adjacent rails, especially those sharing a regulator or a level translator. Back-feeding through I/O protection diodes can show up here as a diode drop in diode-test mode.

items.text: High-voltage and isolation barriers show no continuity across the barrier
items.hint: Measure resistance from primary to secondary side; use an insulation resistance tester at a voltage appropriate to the design and per the safety requirement.

items.text: Bring-up power plan lists each rail's expected voltage and current and the current limit to use
items.hint: Prepare this before power-on from the power tree. It gives every check below a pass/fail reference.

items.text: Battery is not connected for first power-up; a current-limited supply or battery simulator is used instead
items.hint: A battery can deliver very high fault current into a short. Connect the real battery only after the protection and charge paths are verified.

items.text: First power-up uses a bench supply with current limit set just above the expected input current
items.hint: Rule of thumb: start at a limit modestly above the calculated quiescent current, then raise it in steps. Watch for the supply going into current limit.

items.text: Input voltage is ramped slowly from zero while input current is monitored
items.hint: Watch for current rising abnormally before regulators should be active, which indicates a short or reversed part. Stop and investigate any unexpected step.

items.text: Thermal camera or touch check shows no unexpected hot spots within the first seconds of power
items.hint: A thermal camera finds shorted capacitors and back-driven ICs quickly. Compare against expected hot parts (regulators, processors).

items.text: Input current at idle is within the expected range from the power budget
items.hint: Record the value for each board. Large board-to-board spread usually indicates an assembly defect.

items.text: Every rail measures within its specified tolerance at the regulator output and at the far-end load
items.hint: Measure at the load pins as well as the regulator to catch distribution drop. Compare to datasheet tolerance of the load ICs.

items.text: Power-good, status and indicator signals report the expected state
items.hint: Check PGOOD outputs, reset supervisors and status LEDs. A missing power-good often explains a processor that never leaves reset.

items.text: Mains-connected boards are first powered through an isolation transformer with suitable safety precautions
items.hint: Use an isolation transformer, a variac for slow ramp and differential or isolated probes. Follow the lab's high-voltage work procedure.

items.text: Ripple and noise on each rail is within the load ICs' requirements
items.hint: Measure with a short ground spring at the probe tip, bandwidth limit noted, at the load. Long ground leads add pickup and give misleading results.

items.text: Load-step response keeps each rail within tolerance during transients
items.hint: Use an electronic load or a switched resistor at realistic slew rates, or exercise the real firmware load. Check overshoot, undershoot and settling against load IC limits.

items.text: Switching regulator loop stability is acceptable (bode measurement or load-step ringing)
items.hint: Measure phase margin with a loop injection transformer if a test point exists; otherwise judge from load-step ringing. Low margin causes intermittent faults across temperature.

items.text: Power-up sequencing order and timing match the requirements of the sequenced devices
items.hint: Capture all relevant rails and resets on a multi-channel scope at power-on. Compare to processor, FPGA or DDR datasheet sequencing requirements.

items.text: Power-down sequencing does not violate device requirements or back-power any rail
items.hint: Capture rails at power removal. Look for rails held up through I/O pins or slow-discharging outputs.

items.text: Board starts reliably at minimum specified input voltage
items.hint: Test with the worst-case source impedance (cable, battery) where possible. Include inrush current interacting with the source.

items.text: Board starts and operates at maximum specified input voltage
items.hint: Verify no component exceeds its rating and that protection does not trip falsely. Measure peak stress on switching nodes.

items.text: Inrush current at power-on is within source, connector and fuse limits
items.hint: Capture input current with a current probe at the worst-case input voltage. Hot-plugging can produce higher inrush and input voltage spikes than a slow bench ramp.

items.text: Converter efficiency at typical and full load meets the power budget
items.hint: Measure input and output power with accurate meters. Low efficiency points to inductor saturation, wrong frequency or layout problems.

items.text: Over-current, over-voltage and thermal protection trip at the designed thresholds
items.hint: Test each protection feature at limited energy where possible. Confirm recovery behavior (latch-off vs hiccup) matches the design intent.

items.text: Motor or actuator supply holds within limits during start-up, stall and regenerative braking
items.hint: Capture bus voltage while starting, stalling and decelerating the load. Regenerated energy can pump the bus above component ratings.

items.text: Rail and connector temperature rise at full load is acceptable
items.hint: Run at maximum current until temperatures settle and measure copper, connectors and fuses with a thermal camera or thermocouples.

items.text: Every crystal and oscillator starts reliably and runs at the expected frequency
items.hint: Measure with a frequency counter or scope through a buffered output where possible; probing a crystal directly loads it and can stop or pull it.

items.text: Crystal frequency accuracy is within the requirement (load capacitance trimmed)
items.hint: Measure ppm error against a reference. Adjust load capacitors if the offset is systematic; timing-critical radios and RTCs are most sensitive.

items.text: Crystal oscillators start reliably at cold and at minimum supply
items.hint: Check oscillator margin per the MCU vendor's guidance (negative resistance test or start-up over temperature). Marginal crystals fail in the field, not on the bench.

items.text: Clock signal integrity (amplitude, edge rate, jitter) meets the receiver requirements
items.hint: Measure at the receiving device with adequate scope bandwidth. Check jitter for SerDes, ADC and high-speed reference clocks against datasheet limits.

items.text: PLLs lock and report lock status as expected
items.hint: Read lock bits through the debugger or test firmware. Intermittent lock loss is often a supply-noise issue.

items.text: Reset is held until all required rails are stable and released cleanly
items.hint: Scope reset against supplies at power-on and with a slow input ramp. Check for glitches on reset during brown-out.

items.text: Brown-out produces a clean reset and recovery without lock-up
items.hint: Dip input voltage slowly below threshold and back. The board must reset and restart, not hang in a partial state.

items.text: Real-time clock keeps time on backup supply for the required duration
items.hint: Remove main power and confirm the RTC retains time. Measure backup current against the budget.

items.text: Debugger connects to each programmable device through the debug header
items.hint: Confirm the JTAG/SWD chain is detected and IDs read correctly. Failure here is usually a pinout, pull-up or reset strap problem.

items.text: Each device can be programmed and verified through the intended programming path
items.hint: Program and verify readback for MCUs, flash, CPLDs and FPGAs. Note programming time for production planning.

items.text: FPGA configures from its boot flash and reports DONE / configuration status
items.hint: Check the configuration mode straps and that the image boots after a power cycle, not only from JTAG.

items.text: Boot ROM recovery or bootloader path works on a blank or corrupted device
items.hint: Confirm a bricked unit can be recovered in the field or factory without rework.

items.text: Debug console (UART or equivalent) outputs readable text at the configured baud rate
items.hint: A console that works early is the fastest bring-up tool; garbled output usually means a clock or baud configuration error.

items.text: Debug and programming interfaces can be locked or disabled as required for production security
items.hint: Verify the readout protection or debug lock procedure on a sacrificial unit before it is applied to production.

items.text: Every I2C, SPI and UART device responds at its expected address or ID
items.hint: Run a bus scan and read ID registers. Missing devices point to address straps, pull-ups or assembly faults.

items.text: All GPIO, LED, button and control signals toggle and read correctly
items.hint: Use a test firmware to exercise each pin and confirm against the pinout. This catches schematic-to-firmware pin mapping errors early.

items.text: External memory passes a full read/write memory test at rated speed
items.hint: Run a pattern-based memory test (walking ones, address-in-address, random) across the full array, including at temperature corners later.

items.text: DDR training or calibration completes with adequate margin
items.hint: Review read/write eye or training margin reports from the controller or vendor tool. Low margin predicts failures over temperature and production spread.

items.text: High-speed serial links train at the target rate with error-free BER test
items.hint: Run PRBS or vendor link tests for a duration long enough to support the BER target. Capture eye diagrams where tools permit.

items.text: USB enumerates at the intended speed and passes basic transfer tests
items.hint: Check enumeration on several hosts and cables. Verify VBUS behavior and current limits.

items.text: Ethernet link establishes at all supported speeds and passes traffic without errors
items.hint: Check link at each negotiated speed and run a sustained traffic test, watching error counters.

items.text: Display initializes and shows correct image without artifacts, and touch reports accurate coordinates
items.hint: Check color order, orientation, backlight dimming and touch across the full panel area.

items.text: Audio input and output paths work with expected level and no audible noise or distortion
items.hint: Check with a test tone and an audio analyzer if available. Listen at minimum volume for hum and digital whine.

items.text: Motor driver commutates correctly in both directions and current sensing reads accurately
items.hint: Start at reduced supply and current limit. Compare measured phase current against the sensed value.

items.text: Motor driver fault protection (over-current, stall, shoot-through) trips as designed
items.hint: Test with a locked rotor or controlled overload at reduced energy. Confirm the driver recovers as intended.

items.text: External connectors pass signals with correct pinout to mating cables and boards
items.hint: Test with the actual mating harness or board rather than a bench lead. Mirror-image pinouts are a common first-article error.

items.text: Sensors return plausible readings that respond correctly to stimulus
items.hint: Compare against a reference instrument or known stimulus. Check axis orientation and sign for IMUs and similar sensors.

items.text: Noise floor of each analog channel is measured and meets the requirement
items.hint: Capture with inputs shorted or terminated and compute RMS noise or noise density. Compare to the noise budget.

items.text: Offset and gain errors are measured and within the requirement or calibration range
items.hint: Apply known reference inputs at multiple points. Errors beyond the calibration range indicate a design or part issue.

items.text: Linearity across the full input range meets the requirement
items.hint: Sweep the input with a precision source and plot error vs input. Look for clipping near the rails.

items.text: Voltage reference output is within tolerance and stable over warm-up
items.hint: Measure with a meter of better accuracy than the reference. Record drift during warm-up and over temperature later.

items.text: Digital and switching activity does not couple into analog channels
items.hint: Compare noise with processors, radios and switchers active vs idle. Look for spurs at known clock or switching frequencies.

items.text: Amplifier stages are stable with no oscillation under all load conditions
items.hint: Check with step inputs and capacitive loads such as cables. Oscillation may appear only as excess noise or offset on a DMM.

items.text: Sensor front-ends meet accuracy with the actual sensor connected
items.hint: Test with the production sensor and cable rather than a simulator; cable capacitance and leakage affect high-impedance inputs.

items.text: Conducted transmit power at each channel and band is within the requirement
items.hint: Measure at the RF test connector or with a coax pigtail into a spectrum analyzer or power meter, accounting for cable loss.

items.text: Receiver sensitivity meets the requirement at the specified error rate
items.hint: Use a signal generator or radio tester through calibrated attenuation. Compare against the radio vendor's reference figures.

items.text: Antenna match (return loss / VSWR) is acceptable across the band in the final enclosure
items.hint: Measure with a VNA at the antenna feed with the enclosure, battery and nearby cables in place. Tune the matching network as needed and record final values.

items.text: Harmonics and spurious emissions at the conducted port are within the regulatory limits
items.hint: Sweep a wide span on a spectrum analyzer while transmitting at max power. Fix filtering before radiated testing.

items.text: Frequency error of the transmitter is within the radio standard's tolerance
items.hint: Measure carrier frequency offset with a radio tester; trim the crystal load if needed.

items.text: Board-generated noise does not desense the receiver
items.hint: Compare sensitivity with all other subsystems active vs idle. Display, switching regulators and memory clocks are common culprits.

items.text: Radiated performance (TRP/TIS or range test) is acceptable in the final enclosure
items.hint: Run an over-the-air test in a chamber if available, or a documented range test against a reference device.

items.text: Component temperatures at worst-case load and maximum ambient are within ratings with margin
items.hint: Measure at room temperature and extrapolate, or test in a chamber at maximum ambient. Use thermocouples on critical parts for accuracy.

items.text: Thermal testing is done in the final enclosure or a representative airflow condition
items.hint: An open bench board runs much cooler than an enclosed product. Note the enclosure state in the results.

items.text: Thermal shutdown and throttling behave as designed
items.hint: Heat the hot parts deliberately and confirm firmware throttling or hardware shutdown and recovery.

items.text: Touch-accessible surfaces stay within the product's touch-temperature requirement
items.hint: Measure external enclosure surfaces at maximum load and ambient against the applicable safety standard's limits.

items.text: Battery temperature during charge and peak discharge stays within the cell's specified window
items.hint: Place a thermocouple on the cell; nearby heat sources can push the cell out of its charge range.

items.text: Board operates correctly at the minimum and maximum rated ambient temperature
items.hint: Run the functional test in a chamber at each extreme with soak time for thermal equilibrium.

items.text: Board operates at the four corners of supply voltage and temperature
items.hint: Combine minimum and maximum input with cold and hot. Failures often appear only at one corner.

items.text: Temperature cycling causes no intermittent faults or solder joint failures
items.hint: Cycle through the rated range while monitoring function. Inspect suspect joints afterward.

items.text: Board survives vibration and mechanical shock to the product requirement
items.hint: Monitor function during the test where possible. Check heavy parts, connectors and tall capacitors afterward.

items.text: Humidity or condensation exposure does not cause leakage or corrosion failures
items.hint: Test coated and uncoated variants if relevant. High-impedance analog nodes are most sensitive.

items.text: Automotive supply transients (load dump, cold crank, reverse battery) are survived as specified
items.hint: Use a transient generator for the pulses required by the requirement specification. Monitor whether the board must keep running or only survive.

items.text: Unit-to-unit variation is checked across all bring-up boards
items.hint: Run key measurements on every board, not just the golden one, to see the spread before production.

items.text: Long-duration soak test runs without errors, resets or memory leaks
items.hint: Run the full system for an extended period (rule of thumb: at least overnight) with logging.

items.text: Radiated emissions pre-scan shows margin to the applicable limits
items.hint: Scan in a pre-compliance chamber or with near-field probes to identify sources. Margin is needed for lab and unit variation.

items.text: Conducted emissions on power ports are within the applicable limits with margin
items.hint: Measure with a LISN on the power input. Switching regulators and motor drivers are the usual sources.

items.text: Board survives ESD contact and air discharge at all user-accessible points
items.hint: Test with an ESD gun at the levels required by the product's standard. Classify the result (no effect, self-recovery, reset, damage).

items.text: Board tolerates fast transients and surges on external cables as required
items.hint: Apply EFT and surge to power and long signal cables per the target standard. Confirm protection parts are effective.

items.text: Radiated and conducted immunity tests cause no unacceptable performance loss
items.hint: Pre-test with a field probe or injection clamp. Analog and radio performance are the most commonly affected.

items.text: Cables, enclosure and grounding used in pre-compliance match the production configuration
items.hint: Different cables or shielding can invalidate the results. Record the test setup with photos.

items.text: Sleep current in each low-power mode meets the budget
items.hint: Measure with a source meter or power analyzer with sufficient dynamic range; average over several wake cycles. Check every unit, since one leaky part dominates.

items.text: Active and wake-up current profile matches the energy budget
items.hint: Capture a full duty cycle and integrate charge. Long wake times or peripherals left on are common surprises.

items.text: No unintended leakage paths through I/O pins, pull-ups or powered-down peripherals
items.hint: Isolate subsystems one at a time to find which contributes extra sleep current.

items.text: Charge profile (pre-charge, constant current, constant voltage, termination) matches the cell specification
items.hint: Log charge current, voltage and temperature over a full charge cycle and compare to the cell datasheet.

items.text: Charging stops or derates outside the cell's allowed temperature window
items.hint: Test with the NTC simulated cold and hot. Charging a lithium cell out of its temperature range is a safety hazard.

items.text: Battery protection trips correctly for over-charge, over-discharge and over-current
items.hint: Test using a battery simulator or controlled source. Confirm recovery behavior after each trip.

items.text: Fuel gauge or battery voltage reporting is accurate across the discharge curve
items.hint: Compare reported state of charge against coulomb-counted reference during a full discharge.

items.text: Device behaves correctly at low battery: warnings, graceful shutdown, no brown-out loops
items.hint: Discharge slowly to cutoff and confirm the system shuts down cleanly and does not repeatedly reboot.

items.text: Shipping or storage mode current meets the shelf-life requirement
items.hint: Measure current in ship mode and confirm the device wakes only by the intended method.

items.text: Test points needed for production test are accessible on the assembled board
items.hint: Check every test point in the test plan is reachable by pogo pins with parts fitted and not covered by coating or labels.

items.text: Production test procedure has been run on the bring-up boards
items.hint: Run a draft of the test procedure on every unit to confirm pass limits and coverage.

items.text: Pass/fail limits for production tests are set from measured spread, not single units
items.hint: Use the data from all bring-up boards plus design margin to set limits.

items.text: Test fixture design requirements (board outline, tooling holes, keep-outs) are confirmed
items.hint: Share the confirmed requirements with the fixture vendor or contract manufacturer.

items.text: Serialization and traceability (labels, unique IDs, MAC addresses) work end to end
items.hint: Program and read back a unique ID on test units and confirm it reaches the test log.

items.text: Functional test coverage catches the assembly defects seen during bring-up
items.hint: Check each defect found in this build would be detected by the production test.

items.text: Every rework, bodge wire and part change is logged with board serial, description and reason
items.hint: Photograph bodges. Unlogged rework makes later measurements meaningless.

items.text: Each fix is captured as a schematic or layout change request for the next revision
items.hint: Link each rework entry to an ECO or issue so it is not lost when the next revision is started.

items.text: Footprint, silkscreen and assembly drawing errors found during bring-up are recorded
items.hint: Include wrong polarity marks, unclear reference designators and mis-sized pads.

items.text: BOM changes (value changes, substitutions, DNF changes) are recorded and fed back to the BOM owner
items.hint: Update the BOM for the next build so rework does not need to be repeated.

items.text: Firmware workarounds for hardware issues are documented as errata
items.hint: Note any hardware fault masked by firmware so the next revision fixes it or keeps the workaround.

items.text: Open issues are triaged by severity with an owner and a decision for the next revision
items.hint: Decide fix-now, fix-later or accept for each issue before releasing the next revision.

items.text: Bring-up report summarizing results, deviations and open issues is written and reviewed
items.hint: The report should include measured data against requirements and a recommendation on releasing the next revision.
